svg.title: How mean average precision (mAP) is computed, step by step
svg.desc: Animated, three panels. Panel 1: three sample images of a cartoon person-and-dog scene with dashed ground-truth boxes and solid purple detection boxes with score tags. Image A has 2 objects and 3 detections (0.95 on the person, 0.70 on the dog, 0.60 on empty background); image B has 1 object, a person, and 2 detections (0.90 and a duplicate 0.80); image C has 1 object, a dog, and no detection. Panel 2: the 5 detections are taken in score order at an IoU threshold of 0.50, the 4 objects counted as one class. For each, the box is highlighted, its IoU with the object is computed (0.83, 0.91, 0.68, 0.57, 0.04), it is judged a hit or a miss (hit, hit, miss as a duplicate of the already matched person, hit, miss), a chip joins the ranked row, and precision = TP/(TP+FP) and recall = TP/4 are plotted as the points (recall, precision) (0.25, 1.00), (0.50, 1.00), (0.50, 0.67), (0.75, 0.75), (0.75, 0.60). The smoothed, never rising curve then encloses an area of 0.50 × 1.00 + 0.25 × 0.75 = AP 0.69, and the dog in image C is marked never found, which is why recall stops at 0.75. Panel 3: AP is computed at ten IoU thresholds from 0.50 to 0.95 and the bars fall (all ten bars are computed from the drawn boxes); their mean, AP50:95, is about 0.41, and averaging over classes gives mAP. At IoU 0.60 the 0.70 box, with an IoU of 0.57, is no longer a hit, so stricter thresholds lower AP.
svg.text: IoU 0.50 · all 4 objects pooled as one class

g.text: Then, highest score first, match each
to an object in its image.
≥ 0.50 and the person is still unmatched: TP
≥ 0.50 and the person is still unmatched: TP
≥ 0.50, but 0.90 already matched this person: FP
≥ 0.50 and the dog is still unmatched: TP
5 detections ranked by score: TP 3, FP 2
Each adds one point: P = TP/(TP+FP), R = TP/4.
AP is the area under the smoothed curve.
Image C's dog is never found: R stops at 0.75.

svg.text: Grey: raw, one point per detection. Purple: smoothed
so precision never rises. AP = the shaded area.
repeat at 10 IoU thresholds, then per class

g.text: At IoU 0.60 the 0.70 box in image A
(IoU 0.57) is no longer a hit, so

svg.text: Panels 1 and 2 are computed from the drawn boxes, and so are all ten bars in panel 3.
